text: A coracle, left on the bank, light as a basket. {lead} gets in and paddles across without spinning more than twice. On the far side: Willow Sprig.
A bale and a bend, and a bowl that wants lofting. {lead} swings and sends it up over the hedge in one long arc. It lands by some loose change and a gratitude card.
Ripples run out from {lead}'s throw like a good rumour, and the stone raps a reed stem. Something drops out of it: Oak Acorn.
The little round boat wobbles, then settles. {lead} crosses the water with short, careful strokes and lands among the reeds. There is Selkie Pearl.
Sheep at the gate, and no sheep will go first. {lead} comes round the back, low and quiet, and the flock files through. The farmer's thanks: Sheep Wool.
A cheese wheel stuck in a hollow, as they do. {lead} gives it a shove and down the slope it goes, and the hollow gives up Banbury Cake.
{lead} takes a run up and lofts the bowl clean over the verge. Where it comes down: a roll of notes.
The bog water is dark and cold. {lead} ploughs through it with its face down and surfaces holding a roll of notes.
Soft ground, a patient creature, and a lot of worms. {lead} brings up the lot, and under them: a purse, a bit damp.
{lead} shoves the dead trunk over the gap, where it lands with a satisfying thump. You walk across, arms out like a tightrope act.
You cross back over the trunk, arms out. {lead} goes under the stream bank, which is its own business.
{lead} tips the wheel over the lip and it bounds off downhill with great purpose. Where it was sitting: Cooper's Hill Ribbon.
{lead} paddles you across in the little round boat, spinning once for good manners. The far bank is quiet, reedy and yours.
{lead} paddles you back. The boat drifts in a gentle circle the whole way, and nobody mentions it.
A molehill, freshly heaped. {lead} drums a gentle rhythm on the ground and the worms come up to see what the fuss is. Among the soil: a few coins.
